tasks.title: Implement and document email validation
tasks.acceptance_criterion: The package exports a reusable email-validation function that returns true for representative ordinary addresses including "person@example.com", returns false without throwing for malformed strings including "person@" and "@example.com" and for non-string inputs, documents its practical-syntax behavior and examples in README.md, and preserves all existing behavior with the full test suite passing.
tasks.deterministic_validity_check: node -e "const api=require('./src/index.js'); const validate=api.validateEmail; if(typeof validate!=='function') process.exit(1); const cases=[['person@example.com',true],['person@',false],['@example.com',false],[null,false],[42,false]]; for(const [value,expected] of cases){let actual; try{actual=validate(value)}catch(error){process.exit(1)} if(actual!==expected) process.exit(1)}"
patch_requirements: Add one focused reusable validator implementation in src/validateEmail.js and export it through src/index.js.
Return a boolean result for every supplied value and reject non-string inputs without throwing.
Implement practical syntax validation only; do not perform network, mailbox-existence, deliverability, ownership, or identity checks.
Add test/validateEmail.test.js with representative valid, malformed, and non-string cases, including every example named by the ratified spec.
Document the exported validation behavior, practical-syntax boundary, boolean result, and valid and invalid usage examples in README.md.
Preserve the existing formatDate implementation, tests, and package configuration without duplicating or replacing their paths.
